function: MADRL (MAVDC) sets reflecting matrices of wireless-powered IRSs to maximize sensing beampattern gain under a rate constraint; BS precoding (MM) and target matching are not learned (pp. 6, 9).
system: BS ULA 32 antennas, 4 single-antenna users, 5 targets, 3 wireless-powered active IRSs (9x9 elements, EH and amplify-reflect phases); wavelength 0.125 m, 1 MHz (pp. 3, 12).
method: MAVDC: value-decomposed multi-agent DDPG, one actor-critic MLP agent per IRS with a mixing network; centralized training, distributed execution; reinforcement learning with shared global reward (pp. 9-11).
data_channel: Own simulator: LoS plus Rician (K=10) BS-IRS and IRS-user channels, Rayleigh BS-user link, path-loss exponents 2.2/3/4, fixed positions; no dataset (pp. 4, 12).
test_conditions: Same fixed layout (4 users, 3 IRSs, 5 targets) for training and evaluation; sweeps of rate requirement, IRS size, harvesting efficiency, targets, IRS count (pp. 12-14).
baselines: Learned: plain MADDPG (Match-MM-MADDPG, MADDPG), Match-SDR-MADDPG (SDR precoder); scenario variants: passive IRS, radar-only, communication-only; no non-learned RIS design (pp. 12-14).
metrics: Sum beampattern gain (dB) and normalized probing power, communication spectral efficiency, training time, execution time (Figs. 4-9, Table IV, pp. 12-15).
complexity: Big-O orders: matching O(J^3 I^2 + I^3 J^2), MAVDC training O(M)+O(M I^3), execution O(N); Table IV: Match-MM-MAVDC training 1703-4733 s, execution 2.3-4.5 ms for 2-6 IRSs (pp. 11-13).
q1_support: p. 4: "can be modeled by Rician fading"; custom simulator with Rician and Rayleigh fading and own path-loss exponents; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "MADRL only needs to be trained once to handle the following"; this is only a claim, no trained model is tested on an unseen layout or configuration, and the sweeps over rate requirement, IRS size, harvesting efficiency and targets are not stated as tests of a model trained under other values.
q3_support: p. 12: "MAVDC helps to obtain a better reward compared with plain MADDPG"; plain MADDPG is the learned baseline, but the SDR variant, passive-IRS, radar-only and communication-only comparisons all keep a learned IRS design, so no non-learned RIS-design baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "The computation complexity of MAVDC is dominated by the"; Big-O orders for the matching game, the MM precoding and MAVDC (pp. 11-12) and measured training and execution times in Table IV (p. 13).
q5_support: p. 12: "Consider a WP-IRS assisted ISAC system where there"; the evaluation uses the authors' own simulated layout (Table III), and the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 5: the learned part (MAVDC) configures the reflecting matrices of wireless-powered IRSs to maximize the sensing beampattern gain under a communication-rate constraint, i.e. RIS configuration in an ISAC system (area 5 over area 3). Target assignment (matching game) and BS precoding (MM, CVX) are not learned. q3 = 0: Match-SDR-MADDPG changes only the BS precoder solver and keeps the learned IRS design; reviewer may confirm. Wavelength 0.125 m (Table III) is about 2.4 GHz although the text mentions mmWave.
